title: Involution-Based TEM with vil-tprs Security
summary: HCI, one of the very few TEMs with the involution property, has been broken; whether such a mode can also achieve vil-tprs security remains open.

formal_statement.body: Construct a tweakable enciphering mode (TEM) with the involution property that achieves vil-tprs security. HCI, one of the very few TEMs with the involution property, has been broken; the unresolved task is to determine whether the involution property and vil-tprs security guarantees can be achieved simultaneously.

scope.domain: Symmetric-cryptographic design of involution-based tweakable enciphering modes with vil-tprs security.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether an involution-based tweakable enciphering mode can be designed while preserving vil-tprs security guarantees.

citations.label: Breaking the IEEE Encryption Standard -- XCB-AES in Two Queries

progress.summary: The source lists this among its open problems after reporting that its results break HCI, one of the very few TEMs with the involution property. It asks whether an involution-based TEM can preserve vil-tprs security.
citation_labels: Amit Singh Bhati et al., Breaking the IEEE Encryption Standard -- XCB-AES in Two Queries
